notes: Each eval is a simulated learner: a second model plays the persona and talks to the tutor. `opening` is the learner's first message; `attachment` (optional) is a PDF sent with it, as the app sends an uploaded resume. Assertions of kind `code` are checked by grade.mjs, with `args` passed to the check; kind `judge` are judged by a model reading the conversation. `truth` holds the persona's real values for fields the plan depends on (eq, min/max or present); the accuracy checks compare the first brief against it, since that's the one a learner might approve without reading closely.

evals.name: resume-pdf-teacher
evals.prompt: A high school teacher uploads a PDF resume and wants out of the classroom
evals.expected_output: Tutor opens with a short summary of the resume, doesn't ask for what it already says, keeps contact details out, finds the target (instructional design in corporate learning) and proposes a brief changing role and industry.
evals.opening: Here's my resume. I think I'm ready to get out of the classroom.
evals.persona: You are Dana Okafor, 33, a high school biology teacher and science department lead in Sacramento. Your resume is attached and accurate. You want to become an instructional designer at a tech company's learning and development team, and you're fine with remote work. You want to leave teaching at the end of this school year, in June 2027. You can put in 5 hours a week, in 1-hour sessions on weekday evenings. Last summer you started a Coursera instructional design course but stopped when the school year began. You care most about practical, portfolio-ready skills. Reply in 1 to 3 sentences.
